label: rem:planck-reynolds
title: Planck--Reynolds number and the turbulence transition
html:
The substrate parameter q determines the three Reynolds-number variables in the brane fluid: characteristic velocity c_q = 1/(q-1), characteristic grain scale \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} = (q-1)/q, and dynamic viscosity \nu_q = \hbar_q/2 = (q-1)/(2q). The corresponding Planck--Reynolds number is:

  \mathrm{Re}_q
  = \frac{c_q \cdot \hbar_q}{\nu_q}
  = \frac{2}{q-1}.
Regime q \mathrm{Re}_q Character
Classical \to 1^+ \to \infty Fully turbulent
Physical \approx 1.110 \approx 18.2 Transitional
Deep quantum \gg 1 \to 0 Laminar

The substrate parameter functions as an inverse turbulence dial. At q = 1, the Reynolds number diverges and unleashes the full Kolmogorov cascade, but the contact structure collapses and particle states vanish.

The laminar--turbulent boundary emerges at \mathrm{Re}_q \sim 1, corresponding to q \sim 3. Active Kelvin modes require [k]_q \leq \mathrm{Re}_q^{1/2}. At the physical anchor q \approx 1.110, this constraint dictates a cutoff k_{\max} \approx 4.
